title: Tangents to a circle
examples: Teacher, if I draw a tangent and a radius, what is the angle between them?
What if I have two tangents drawn from the same point outside the circle?
Can you show me an example where the two tangents have different lengths?

explain.say: Today we learn about tangents to a circle. A tangent touches the circle at exactly one point. This point is called the point of contact.

draw.text: Tangent touches circle at one point.

explain.say: The first key rule is about the angle. A tangent line always meets the radius at a right angle. This means the angle is ninety degrees.
Let us look at an example. If we draw a radius and a tangent, they form a right angle. This is a very important fact to remember.
Next, we look at two tangents from one point. If you draw two tangents from the same outside point, they must have equal lengths. This is another useful rule.
Consider a point outside the circle. If you draw two tangents to it, the segment lengths are always the same. This helps us find unknown lengths easily.

faq.q: Does the radius always meet the tangent at a right angle?
faq.a: Yes, the radius drawn to the point of contact is always perpendicular to the tangent line. This forms a ninety-degree angle.
asks: What is the angle between radius and tangent?

faq.q: If I draw two tangents from the same point, are they equal?
faq.a: Yes, the lengths of the two tangents drawn from the same external point are always equal in length. This is a key property.
asks: Do the tangents have the same length?

faq.q: What if the point is on the circle itself?
faq.a: If the point is on the circle, there is only one tangent, and the radius drawn to that point is perpendicular to it.
asks: What happens at the point of contact?
Does the rule change if I use the circle's edge?

faq.q: Can I use the right angle rule with trigonometry?
faq.a: Yes, because you have a right-angled triangle, you can use sine, cosine, or tangent ratios to find missing sides or angles.
asks: Can I use trig functions here?
Is this useful for finding angles?

faq.q: Does the center of the circle matter for the equal tangents rule?
faq.a: The center is what defines the radius, but the equal tangents rule only depends on the external point and the circle itself. It always holds true.
asks: Does the center point affect the length?
Is the center needed for this proof?

facts: A tangent touches a circle at exactly one point.
The radius drawn to the point of contact is perpendicular to the tangent.
Two tangents drawn from the same external point are equal in length.
If two lines are perpendicular, the angle between them is ninety degrees.

quiz.say: A radius and a tangent meet at a point. What is the angle formed?
quiz.show: Angle formed by radius and tangent?
quiz.why: The radius is always perpendicular to the tangent at the point of contact, which means the angle is ninety degrees.

wrong.0: This might happen if you incorrectly assume the angle is supplementary to the right angle.
wrong.1: This would mean the tangent and radius lie on the same straight line, which is not the case.
wrong.3: This is a common mistake because many angles in geometry are forty-five degrees.

quiz.say: From an outside point P, two tangents are drawn to a circle. If one tangent is five units long, how long is the other?
quiz.show: Two tangents from a point P
quiz.why: The rule states that the two tangents drawn from the same external point must have equal lengths.

wrong.1: This mistake might come from adding the lengths together incorrectly.
wrong.2: This confuses the length of the tangent with the radius length.
wrong.3: While angles matter for other calculations, the lengths themselves are fixed and equal.

quiz.say: If you form a right triangle using the center, the external point, and the tangent point, which side is the tangent?

options.show: the side connecting the external point to the circle
options.say: the side connecting the external point to the circle

options.show: the line from the center to the external point
options.say: the line from the center to the external point

quiz.why: The tangent forms one of the sides of the right triangle, connecting the external point to the point of contact.

wrong.1: The radius is always opposite the right angle or forms the other leg, not the tangent itself.
wrong.2: This line is the hypotenuse, not the tangent side.
wrong.3: The tangent is one of the two legs, not the longest side (hypotenuse).
